Dum Biryani design directions

Frontend work from 17 to 23 September 2026.

Every screenshot on this page was taken from software running on the development machine on 23 September 2026. Phone screens were captured at 393 by 852 points. Nothing here is a drawing or a mock-up.

1. Website

Replaced

Options shown

None. Work started on a React website on 17 September 2026 and stopped the same day, before any design was drawn.

Picked

Nothing was picked. The brief changed to a phone app for iPhone and Android, so the website files were deleted and replaced by an app project on 17 September 2026.

Screenshots

None. The website only ever showed the default starter page, and the files were deleted before the project was saved to version control, so there is nothing left to run. Rebuilding it would mean writing new code, which would not be a screenshot of what existed.

2. App looks

Current

Five versions of the app were designed between 17 and 23 September 2026. Each one is a working demo that runs in a browser and covers the same screens: home, menu, dish, bag, and order tracking. Each also has one extra screen of its own.

All five use the same colours (dark brown, saffron, maroon), the same 12 dishes, and the same prices in rupees. The photographs are free stock images used as placeholders.

Options shown

  • Poster. Dish names in tall narrow capitals, one dish per screen. You swipe up for the next dish and hold the button to add it to the bag.
  • Nizam. A magazine on maroon pages, with a large serif. Three sections you swipe sideways: the kitchen, the menu, the restaurants.
  • Ember. A dark screen lit from below, one dish at a time. You drag the dish name to stretch the letters, spin a dial to change dish, and hold the pot to lift its lid.
  • Index. A light layout on a strict grid, with very large numbers for prices and cooking times. The only version on a pale background.
  • Reel. Photography first. The word "Dum" is cut out of a dark layer so the food shows through the letters, and the screen zooms through a letter to move on.

Picked

None yet. This is the decision waiting on you. The recommendation is Ember, with the menu and tab bar from Index. All five demos are still live.

On 23 September 2026 all five were corrected: text was running off the edge of the screen in 9 places across 4 of the demos. The screenshots below are from the corrected versions.

3. App project

Built, then parked

The iPhone and Android project was set up on 17 September 2026 using Expo. It holds the colours, the text sizes and four tabs. The screens are placeholders with three dishes typed in by hand. No design has been built into it yet, because the look has not been picked.

These two screenshots are that project running in a browser on 23 September 2026. It uses the phone's own light colours here, not the brand colours.

Decisions needed

  1. Which of the five looks to build. The recommendation is Ember.
  2. Dark screens only, or a light version as well. Index is the light one.
  3. Food photographs: pay for a shoot, or use computer-generated images. The demos use free stock photos, and they do not match each other.
  4. Which features go in the first release. The full list runs to about 40, including delivery, collection, table booking, loyalty points, catering and gift cards.
  5. Whether to save the current work to version control. At the moment none of it is committed, so nothing can be recovered if the machine is lost.
  6. Confirm the first city and payment methods. The demos assume Pakistan, with rupees, JazzCash and Easypaisa.
